data.title: Leopold Aschenbrenner's Fund Blowup Rumor Unconfirmed; Q3 Holdings Report Expected November 16
data.description:
Reports that Situational Awareness, the investment fund founded by Leopold Aschenbrenner, has suffered another blowup have not been confirmed. According to Odaily, Leopold Stock Tracker said there is no confirmed source for the rumor, while the fund’s disclosed second-quarter holdings have since declined significantly. SanDisk fell about 63% from a reference price near $836; Micron dropped about 41%, Core Scientific 56%, Nebius 54%, CoreWeave 55% and Bloom Energy 43% under the cited tracking methodology.

The fund’s third-quarter 13F report is expected to be released on November 16, disclosing its U.S. stock holdings as of September 30 and covering changes from July 1 through September 30.

data.title: California Billionaire Tax Measure Likely to Fail, Setback for Wealth-Tax Push Nationwide
data.description:
California voters were projected to reject Proposition 40, the first U.S. proposal to tax billionaires, bringing a costly and deeply divisive political battle in the state to a close. According to Sina Finance, citing DDHQ’s post on X, 46% of voters supported the measure and 54% opposed it, with about 71% of ballots counted.

The measure would have imposed a one-time 5% wealth tax on assets held by billionaires living in California at the beginning of 2026, with most of the revenue used to shore up healthcare funding. Its defeat is a major setback for nationwide efforts to tax large fortunes; supporters had hoped California would provide a model for similar campaigns elsewhere in the United States.

Opponents included tech billionaires, Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom and California Planned Parenthood affiliates. They raised more than $300 million, with the leading group, Build Better California, funded by Google co-founder Sergey Brin and other ultra-high-net-worth individuals.

A healthcare union first proposed the tax more than a year ago to offset federal budget cuts that could force multiple hospitals to close and leave millions of Californians without health insurance. Supporters included Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Ro Khanna, whose district includes Silicon Valley. At a news conference as voting ended, Khanna said, “Billionaires must be taxed. We will achieve this goal, we will succeed, and we can defeat capital.” The proposal divided Democrats and labor groups.

data.title: Tom Lee Says AI Investment Boom Is Far From Over as Compute Shortages May Lift Prices
data.description: Tom Lee, chairman of Bitcoin treasury company Bitmine, said in an interview with CNBC that the AI investment boom is far from over. According to Odaily, Lee said increased use of tokens could drive continued growth in demand for computing resources, tightening supply again and pushing related prices higher. He said bottlenecks in AI infrastructure could return to focus. Many U.S. states and local communities welcome the economic benefits of AI investment but also seek to shape projects according to local conditions and strengthen AI safety oversight.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Meta Chief Strategy Officer Dave Wehner Leaves for CFO Role at Fireworks
data.description: Dave Wehner confirmed on Friday that he would leave Meta to become chief financial officer of AI inference startup Fireworks. According to Sina Finance, he joined Facebook in 2012 as vice president of corporate finance and business planning, became CFO in 2014, held the role for more than eight years, and became chief strategy officer in 2022. Before joining Facebook, Wehner was CFO of Zynga and a managing director at investment bank Allen & Company. He also serves on the board of autonomous trucking technology company Aurora Innovation.

data.title: Anthropic Still Plans Pre-Thanksgiving IPO, Targeting Up to $1.75 Trillion Valuation
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing the Financial Times, Anthropic plans to move ahead with an IPO before U.S. Thanksgiving, targeting a valuation of $1.25 trillion to $1.75 trillion and proceeds of $80 billion to $100 billion. The expected midpoint is about $1.5 trillion, below the $2 trillion some investors had previously anticipated, as technology stocks face a steep sell-off.

Investors familiar with the matter said Anthropic hopes to list on schedule even if it must accept a lower valuation. The company’s third-quarter revenue grew nearly 50% to about $17 billion, while its latest annualized revenue run rate was about $81 billion, up from $65 billion at the end of July.

Anthropic plans to spend about $900 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure over the coming years. It currently has nearly $150 billion in cash and liquid investments. JPMorgan is expected to hold a briefing for potential investors on November 13.

data.title: Apple Says More Than 100,000 Apps Are Now Compatible With iPhone Duo
data.description:
Apple said software support for iPhone Duo is improving quickly, with more than 100,000 apps built specifically for the device now available in the App Store and thousands of newly adapted apps added daily. According to Sina Finance, more than a dozen major apps have updated for iPhone Duo, including Microsoft Word, Outlook, Zoom, NBA and NHL sports apps, Etsy, LTK, Goodnotes, Extra and Halide Mark III; Netflix, YouTube, Instagram and WhatsApp were already compatible.

Apps that have not been adapted display black bars along the sides of the screen, reducing usable display space, and may place some features in a “More” menu. Apple said more than 2,000 developers took part in over 50 in-person workshops across 19 cities, where they could try iPhone Duo and receive technical support to adapt their apps.

The 256GB iPhone Duo starts at $1,999, and demand has exceeded Apple’s expectations. The device sold out within hours of presale opening, and delivery estimates now extend into next year. During this week’s earnings call, Apple said it could not yet estimate when supply constraints would ease.

Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of worldwide developer relations, said the company was pleased to see developers embrace iPhone Duo so quickly and thanked them for their creativity and innovation. She said the response had exceeded expectations and that Apple looked forward to faster updates as more apps are adapted.

data.title: US MARKET CLOSE | Mixed Close as Chip Stocks Rebound, Microsoft Winds Down Oracle AI Computing Deal
data.description: U.S. stocks stabilized Friday with the three major indexes closing mixed. Dip-buying buoyed the market as chip stocks rebounded, offsetting concerns that the Federal Reserve will hike rates in December. The Dow fell 237.32 points, or 0.46%, to 51,285.73; the S&P 500 rose 23.13 points, or 0.31%, to 7,376.86; and the Nasdaq gained 264.42 points, or 1.09%, to 24,579.42, according to Sina Finance. Among the "Magnificent Seven," Tesla rose 4.23%, Nvidia gained 2.78%, Meta Platforms added 0.84%, Google rose 0.78%, Amazon fell 0.35%, Apple declined 0.52%, and Microsoft dropped 0.99%. Semiconductors led gains, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 4.21%. AMD surged over 11%, Intel over 7%, TSMC over 6%, and Qualcomm and ASML over 5%. Concerns over a potential slowdown in data center construction had hammered U.S. stocks on Thursday, wiping out $1 trillion in combined market value from the "Magnificent Seven" in a single day. Democratic lawmakers called for curbing data center expansion after sweeping elections. Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa said in an interview, "We will craft laws to protect Texans, and until those protections are in place, we need to stop data center construction." Chris Grisanti of MAI Capital Management said investor concerns may persist since Hinojosa and others will not take office until January, but he remained optimistic about AI, believing construction-related deals will eventually close. Friday's optimism was tempered by reports that Microsoft is gradually terminating its arrangement to rent AI computing power from Oracle, having fueled the "new cloud" boom through major contracts with CoreWeave, Nscale, and Nebius. Oil prices ticked higher, with December WTI crude rising 31 cents to $90.83 per barrel, up 0.34%, and January Brent up 3 cents to $98.32 per barrel, up 0.03%. The S&P 500 energy index posted a double-digit weekly decline. Investors also digested the latest nonfarm payroll report, which showed 165,000 jobs added in October, well above expectations. The unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, indicating labor market resilience. FedWatch data showed traders increased bets on a Fed rate hike as early as next month, with the December hike probability rising to 78% from 70%.

data.title: ASIA NIGHT SESSION | TAIEX Futures Reclaim 40,000 in Night Trade, Nikkei Futures Gain 840 Points
data.description:
According to Kabutan, HKET and SET News, markets remained concerned about tighter regulation of artificial intelligence and data center construction after the U.S. Democratic Party won control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections. U.S. nonfarm payrolls rose by 165,000 in October, well above the 59,000 forecast, while the unemployment rate fell to 4.1% from 4.2%, reinforcing expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December. U.S. chip stocks rebounded on Friday, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index closing up 4.21% and TSMC's ADR rising 6.33%.

Japanese index futures rose in night trade. The Osaka Exchange's December 2026 Nikkei 225 futures ended the night session at 58,250, up 840 points and 815.23 points above the Nikkei Stock Average's cash close of 57,434.77, on volume of 23,614 contracts. TOPIX futures rose 79 points to 3,779.

Hang Seng Index night futures closed up 148 points at 24,647. HKEX data showed November Hang Seng Index futures traded between 24,328 and 24,694 in the after-hours session, on volume of 21,168 contracts. The NASDAQ Golden Dragon China Index rose 1.7% to 5,843. Among ADRs, Alibaba's U.S. shares were equivalent to HK$107.29, 2.28% above the Hong Kong close; Meituan's ADR was at HK$81.21, up 1.00%; Tencent's ADR was at HK$420.81, up 0.24%; and the HSBC ADR was at HK$136.55, down 0.69%.

TAIEX futures rose 646 points, or 1.63%, to close the night session at 40,298, back above the 40,000 level. TSMC futures gained NT$40 in the night session. The TAIEX fell 1,873.08 points, or 4.51%, to close at 39,701.64 in the previous session.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Leopold Aschenbrenner's Fund Falls 67% as AI Infrastructure Stocks Slide

data.title: predict.fun Puts 76ers' Win Probability at 59% Against Cavaliers as Philadelphia Seeks Sixth Straight Win
data.description:
predict.fun's event market puts the Philadelphia 76ers' probability of beating the Cleveland Cavaliers in their NBA Cup group-stage game at 59%. According to Odaily, the teams are scheduled to play in Cleveland today at 8:30 a.m. in the 2026-27 NBA Cup group stage.

The 76ers enter with an 8-1 record, the best in the league, and a five-game winning streak. Cleveland is 4-4 and has lost two consecutive games. In their first meeting this season, Philadelphia overcame a 29-point deficit to beat the Cavaliers 114-106.

James, Embiid, Maxey and Jalen Brown were not listed on the 76ers' pregame injury report. Backup center Bona is out with a neck injury, while Barlow and Hukporti are also unavailable. For Cleveland, Jarrett Allen is out with a right knee contusion. Peyton Watson and Tyrese Proctor are available, while Jaylon Tyson remains out.

The game also marks James' first return to Cleveland as a member of the 76ers.

data.title: Citigroup Shelves Autokiniton’s $1 Billion Loan Deal
data.description:
Autokiniton U.S. Holdings has shelved a proposed amendment and extension of an approximately $1.05 billion leveraged loan. According to Sina Finance, a person familiar with the matter said the source requested anonymity because the information was confidential. The company had revised the proposed terms, shortening the maturity by one year to 2030, setting the price at 97.5 cents on the dollar, and setting the interest rate at 4.75 percentage points above the benchmark, the top of the initial discussion range.

Investors are seeking greater concessions on financing and refinancing deals for highly indebted companies amid market volatility. The United States completed only four leveraged loan issuances this week. Traders are assessing the potential effect of a Democratic sweep in the midterm elections on AI infrastructure projects that rely on borrowing to expand.

A KPS Capital spokesperson declined to comment. Citigroup, the lead arranger, and Autokiniton had not responded to inquiries.
